title: Espagnole Sauce (Brown Sauce)
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, made with a brown roux, mirepoix, tomato purée, and rich brown stock to create a deep, robust foundation for demi-glace and many traditional meat sauces.

items: 500 ml (2 cups) brown stock (veal or beef)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and cook, whisking constantly, until a deep golden-brown roux forms.
Add the diced carrot, onion, and celery, then sauté until lightly caramelized.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2–3 minutes to deepen the flavor and reduce acidity.
Gradually whisk in the hot brown stock until smooth and well combined.
Add the bouquet garni and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 45–60 minutes, skimming any impurities from the surface as needed.
Remove the bouquet garni and strain the sauce through a fine sieve or chinois.
Adjust seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper before serving.
chefTips: Caramelize the roux and mirepoix properly to achieve a rich, complex flavor.
Use high-quality homemade brown stock for authentic results.
Simmer gently rather than boiling to maintain a smooth texture.
Espagnole is the foundation for Demi-Glace, Bordelaise, and Chasseur sauces.
Ideal for roasted meats, braised dishes, steaks, and hearty stews.
